compiled_state.description:
## Observation

`rebar store fsck --repair` on 2026-10-28 (bug df72 store repair) committed a3-remediation batch 1, then stopped every remaining batch:

```
a3-remediation: pre-tag pre-a3-remediation @ ebb822a0a914
a3-remediation: reconciler paused
ABORT: push failed for batch 1: To https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git
 ! [rejected]                HEAD -> tickets (non-fast-forward)
```

Other sessions push to `tickets` every few minutes, so on the live store a multi-batch remediation will usually lose this race. 30 fsck issues stayed unrepaired.

## Cause (code)

`_commit_repair_batch` in `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` publishes each batch with a bare `git push origin HEAD:tickets`: no fetch, no merge, no retry. A rejection appends `ABORT` and returns False, which ends the run. It also hardcodes `origin` rather than the configured `tickets.remote`. The store's normal write path recovers from the same rejection by merging the remote and retrying (`_store/sync.py` push recovery).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A rejected non-fast-forward push of a remediation batch is reconciled with the remote and retried through the store's shared push path, instead of aborting the run.
- [ ] The push uses the configured tickets remote and branch, not a literal `origin`/`tickets`.
- [ ] A test pushes a concurrent commit to the remote between batches and asserts every batch lands.
- [ ] A failure that stays unresolved after the bounded retry still aborts with a message naming the batch.
compiled_state.title: fsck --repair aborts remaining remediation batches on a rejected push instead of reconciling and retrying
